# googleworkspace_license_assignment (Resource)

License Assignment resource in the Terraform Googleworkspace provider. It assigns a Google Workspace product SKU license to a user.

This resource uses these OAuth scopes. The provider's default scopes do not include `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/apps.licensing`, and `oauth_scopes` replaces the default list, so set `oauth_scopes` to all the scopes that your configuration needs:

- `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/apps.licensing` (always).
- `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user.readonly` or `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user` (to store `directory_user_id`, to follow a renamed user, to check a change to `user_id`, and to find the user of the license assignment by `directory_user_id` before a refresh, a delete or a SKU change). With `directory_user_id` set, each refresh makes one Directory API request for each license assignment. Without this scope, or if the admin role of the principal cannot read users, `directory_user_id` stays empty and the resource uses only the License Manager API with the address in `user_id`: a refresh that does not find the license lists the product by `user_id` to find another SKU of the user, and removes the resource from state if it finds none; a delete that does not find the license treats it as gone; a change to `user_id` replaces the license assignment. A renamed user is not followed: the refresh removes the license assignment from state, a destroy does not remove the license, and the next apply tries to assign the license again and fails with a `412` error because the user already has it. Import the license assignment with the user's new address to recover. If `directory_user_id` is set and the scope is later removed, a refresh that does not find the license, a delete and a SKU change fail with an error that names the scope.
- `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.customer.readonly` or `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.customer` (only if `customer_id` is `my_customer`).

A create or a SKU change that gets a `412 Precondition Failed` error fails at once and is not retried. For a create, the two likely causes are:

- The user already has a license for this product, possibly with a different SKU. A user can have only one SKU of a product, and Google Workspace can assign a license automatically. Import the existing license assignment with the ID `<product_id>/<sku_id>/<user_id>`. Any SKU of the product works in the import ID, because the refresh finds the user's current SKU. Then set `sku_id` to the SKU that you want.
- The SKU has no free seats. Make licenses available, then apply again.

For a SKU change, the likely cause is that the new SKU has no free seats.

Other behavior to know:

- The resource stores the user's immutable Directory user ID in `directory_user_id`. If it is set, a refresh, a delete and a SKU change find the user by this ID and use the user's current primary email address, so they follow a rename (also when the old address is no longer an alias) and never act on a different user that now has the address in `user_id`. If the user does not exist any more, a refresh removes the resource from state, a delete treats the license as gone, and a SKU change fails. `user_id` keeps the configured value. `directory_user_id` is set when the License Manager API or the Directory API finds `user_id` as the user's primary address: at create, at import, or at the first refresh of state from before this attribute. Until then, an address that the Directory API finds only as an alias is treated as not found.
- If the SKU is changed outside Terraform, a refresh finds the user's current SKU of the product and the plan changes `sku_id` back in place. The resource is removed from state only if the user has no license for the product. To find the SKU, the refresh lists the license assignments of the product once for each provider configuration, which can take time for a large customer. With `directory_user_id` set, a delete that does not find the license with the stored SKU also lists the product, and deletes the user's license of the product with its current SKU. If that listing fails, or without `directory_user_id`, such a delete treats the license as gone.
- If a refresh finds that the user was renamed, it reports a warning with the user's current primary email address. Set `user_id` to that address.
- If the Directory API refuses a user lookup (a `403` error, or no answer within 15 seconds), the optional user lookups (to store `directory_user_id`, and for a refresh without it) are skipped for the rest of the provider configuration. A delete or a SKU change with `directory_user_id` set still looks up the user, and fails if the lookup fails.
- A change to `user_id` is done in place, with no API write, only if the plan confirms that the new value is the current primary email address of the user in `directory_user_id`, and the License Manager API returns the assignment for the new address. If the new address belongs to a different user or has no license, the change replaces the license assignment. If the new address is an alias of the user, the plan fails, because `user_id` must be the primary address. If the check fails for another reason, for example a missing scope, the plan fails. A rename of `googleworkspace_user.primary_email` in the same apply as the license assignment cannot be confirmed at plan time, because the user is not renamed yet, so it replaces the license assignment. To keep the license, apply the rename first with the old `user_id`, then change `user_id`.
- The create retries a `404` error or a `400 User email not valid` error until the create timeout, because a new user is not immediately visible to the License Manager API. A typo in `user_id` therefore fails only when the create timeout ends.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0

# The licensing scope is not a default scope. Add it to oauth_scopes, together
# with the scopes that your other resources need.
provider "googleworkspace" {
  customer_id = "A01b123xz"
  oauth_scopes = [
    "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/admin.directory.user",
    "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/apps.licensing",
  ]
}

resource "googleworkspace_user" "dwight" {
  primary_email = "dwight.schrute@example.com"
  password      = "34819d7beeabb9260a5c854bc85b3e44"
  hash_function = "MD5"

  name {
    family_name = "Schrute"
    given_name  = "Dwight"
  }
}

# Google Workspace Business Starter
resource "googleworkspace_license_assignment" "dwight" {
  product_id = "Google-Apps"
  sku_id     = "1010020027"
  user_id    = googleworkspace_user.dwight.primary_email
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `product_id` (String) The product's unique identifier, for example `Google-Apps`. See [Products and SKUs](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/licensing/v1/how-tos/products).
- `sku_id` (String) The product SKU's unique identifier, for example `1010020027`. See [Products and SKUs](https://developers.google.com/workspace/admin/licensing/v1/how-tos/products). A change reassigns the user to the new SKU of the same product in place.
- `user_id` (String) The user's primary email address. A change replaces the license assignment, unless the plan confirms that the new address is the same user with the same license.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `directory_user_id` (String) The user's immutable unique ID in the Directory API. The provider uses it to find the user of the license assignment after a rename, and to never act on a different user.
- `etag` (String) ETag of the resource.
- `id` (String) ID of the license assignment, in the format `<product_id>/<sku_id>/<user_id>`.
- `product_name` (String) Display name of the product.
- `self_link` (String) Link to this license assignment in the API.
- `sku_name` (String) Display name of the product SKU.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String)
- `delete` (String)
- `update` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# Copyright (c) HashiCorp, Inc.
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0

# The ID is <product_id>/<sku_id>/<user_id>
terraform import googleworkspace_license_assignment.dwight Google-Apps/1010020027/dwight.schrute@example.com
```
